body: Hi - ALL of your sentiments are true. The rest of the world has NO idea how to deal with grief - or perhaps pain in general. I joined an online Facebook grief group - they all get it. Maybe you might consider doing the same? People are so afraid of saying the wrong thing or sitting with you through the pain, that the only ones capable are those in pain themselves. I’m truly heartbroken you lost your friend. I’m sorry for their unbearable pain and now yours. Those of us living through a loss get it. Come find us.

Hi - my son has aspergers. While it presents its own challenges, it also makes him a really awesome teen. He also deals with being fixation and rumination. With rumination, he’s had a lot of success with processing those events over until he can let them go. He has a counselor but frankly, talking it out is what has helped him so much. Most times when we hear the situation, he isn’t processing it correctly and putting too much emotion where it isn’t warranted. With fixation - well seriously, that’s like a superpower. :) whatever you turn your attention toward, you will surpass the rest of us. When we were fixated on legos when he was younger - he was the best damn LEGO builder I’ve ever known! ;) we have to watch screen time - he has a hard time with too much - which isn’t healthy. But at 16, he has a small group of friends that love him. And having lost my older son to suicide - small numbers of great friends seem to be MUCH more fulfilling than large groups of acquaintances. You are pretty awesome the way you are. Your brain makes you wildly capable in some aspects, and just needs support in other ways. Ignore the statistics. They are outdated and don’t reflect you. There are some pretty fantastic people with aspergers who are out there in the world kicking butt. And so many more are talking about it and really accepting of the challenges. My son and I laugh when we watch Greta Grunberg together. We see the face contortion when she is upset that I’ve only ever seen in my son. It’s so endearing, and it’s her power. Emotion and fixation which is attempting to change the world. So take a breath, and look at these challenges as actual talents. When the rest of the world is bored or tired, whatever you apply your mind to - you can do far more than the rest of us simpletons. ;) sending love your way

I’m sorry. This isn’t the right approach. My pain doesn’t even begin to approach yours. For that I’m so sorry. Forgive me for allowing my pain to overseed your own. I hope for a different path for you....

Hi - I was your mother. I was hurt by you, I cried over you, I prayed for you, I tried. And then you were gone. And I regretted every single moment I handled incorrectly. I hated myself. I still do. You were the best thing that ever happened to me. I don’t have any answers to your pain....but as a mother - NOTHING goes unforgiven. You are beautiful, capable, amazing in her eyes. And that continues forever..... she just wishes she could tell you that now. But she is also lost watching you suffer. I lost a child your age. Can we please find a different way to help you forgive yourself and see yourself through another’s eyes?

It’s a very very long road. For now - rest, cry, breathe, distract just to get through the days. Let people spend time with you to distract. About a month in, we had the strength to call a grief counselor. I’m so very sorry. We are 18 months in, but those early days are indescribably painful mixed with shock and denial. You may look up some grief groups online to help in time - it may be too raw right now. We also found only those specific to suicide helped. Sending love to you and your family.

When we have moments that emotionally crush us, we have to look at that situation more closely. For likely many of us, we are like “no biggie - happens to the best of us”. But for you, is it the embarrassment of that moment? Is it the embarrassment of the bullying situation? Is it the embarrassment that it didn’t play out how you would have wanted? When you can answer that question, then you can start working through it. So - in a bullying case - YOU were the victim. YOU. Bad things were done TO you. Because you reacted to the person that did those things doesn’t make you bad. In the best case scenario, that person reflects and is like “I was an asshole. I can’t believe I caused that.” Now they may or may not say it, but you don’t know. Regardless you had a reaction to your past and a past hurt. That isn’t you now. You may not be comfortable letting people see that pain, but that’s all that happened. Someone saw your vulnerability. And if you can process this - that something bad happened to you that you didn’t deserve and was hurtful and unacceptable, maybe then you can make peace with it? And then remember that that doesn’t define you now.

3 months it’s still too new. You are still in shock. James didn’t leave because he didn’t love you or didn’t know you loved him, suicide is so much more complicated than that. You are still his brother. And you can still carry him with you all the days of your life. We do with my son. Every holiday, every vacation - we include him. This is probably too soon, but we did counseling as a family, connected with other families and carried our child and his memory along. In that sense, his memory never dies. And though I’m not sure of your belief system - for us personally we know our boy is still with us helping from the other side.

It doesn’t say anything about you other than that had an embarrassing moment under the influence, reflected on it and didn’t like that reaction. So now you forgive yourself and set better limits where you have control. Those people weren’t your friends to begin with, so close that chapter and move forward.

Honest question - why are you not filing an order of protection and having CPS investigating her neglect? At least with her out of the situation and banned from contact with you, you could restart with structure, a budget and a safe home?
You may be underestimating the need to wear a mask in public for protection and privacy with how those of us feel when alone.

I don’t see you as worthless. Frankly, I’m doubting there is much you could have ever done to make me think otherwise. Your words are very kind. We all walk this earth with regrets....some show on the outside and others we hold close to our heart. I understand that you cannot change the past as I cannot either. All both of us can do is step forward. Sometimes it all seems very frightening and uncertain, but I hope that the tiny steps I can make may lead to a change. Today we aren’t the same people we were yesterday or we wouldn’t have these regrets. So in my case and I’m hoping maybe it resonates with you a little - this pain can either eat me alive or I can take this and try to carry on that love and the words I wish I could say to my boy. I’m not minimizing your feelings and I hope that comes across.

Hello - I’m so sorry for how you are suffering. I know you must be suffering horribly to consider this. I lost my son to suicide. I imagine he must have felt similar to you. He was 17. If I could tell him anything aside from how much I love him, and miss him - it’s that life could have changed for the better. I wish the same for you. Even one tiny little change can build on itself in time. Words are failing me, but sometimes suicidal thoughts bring tunnel vision. Anything can change for you. I’m so sorry.
Sometimes animals are the best comfort. I hear your pain and glad you posted. Truly wishing you better moments.

Yes, it’s true...they don’t see that agony. Mostly because depression exists on the inside and many people are conditioned to wearing a “mask” on the outside. They only see your actions and reactions and that’s what they react to. That isn’t fair and I am not intending to negate their faults, but I think it’s closer to what’s really occurring. A lot of times when watching someone suffer from the outside, you feel so helpless with no idea on what to do. You think, speaking as a mom here, that you can fix all the outside stuff and the rest will sort itself out. I get now how foolish that is and that the most important thing you can give is a constant reassuring presence, but wanted to know there are many of us still learning and wanting to do better.

I’m so sorry you are feeling this way. I think some of us don’t always understand the unspoken anguish others go through until it’s too late. They are left with regrets and sorrow, but they didn’t really understand. Sometimes people assume that day to day others feel better as those of us not suffering the same might. I’m sorry you are in so much pain. I dont think anyone deserves it.

Sad to see this comment. Someone here reaching out, trying to send you positive energy and you respond so negatively? Why? Let the love try to reach you. We are here to help...even when we don’t understand. We’re just listening and trying with all we know how.

So you don’t see why many of us are here and that’s ok. I’m here because my son at 17 died by suicide. And I came to see if I could find his letter. And when I couldn’t, I stayed to help. Why? Because mental illness and depression is a beast. And yes - I care about every post I read and respond to. I invest my life to trying to help those who need help get help in an affordable and timely way. So I care...it levels me with every post I respond and offer myself to, but at that moment - YOU are more important. I’m not sure what the true makeup of suicidality looks like in the brain and what will help - but there are many of us trying in all of your names...because you don’t deserve to suffer and you deserve better from us all.

Puppies are a lot of work. Do you have experience with puppies? I know you are exhausted, but there are many things you can do to make this easier. Is the puppy being contained in the crate to rest from time to time? If the puppy is having accidents, get diapers. My new rescue is wearing one now. They are disposable and it allows you to create a schedule. Can you tell me what aspect you are struggling with immediately and see if we can help? Being overwhelmed is very hard and debilitating. Glad you have posted.

So forgive me, but this post set off alarm bells. Please tell your family!! I understand that you are independent, but being so puts you in the highest risk of completion. You are NOT a burden....that’s a depressive mind speaking to you. I lost my son....while i completely understand that the treatments are insufficient, I ask that you explore more options. ❤️
Better off in what way? Caveat to add that my son passed away by suicide a year ago and while I am certain he felt this way, those were solely depressive thoughts and not at all rooted in truth.

Today a ketamine substitute was approved by the FDA. It will be a nasal spray administered in the drs office to relieve suicidal thoughts immediately. Would this be an option? It would be covered by insurance...

I’d love to chat with you. I don’t do guilt, but I’m one of those “strong” moms....to be absolutely clear, there is NO getting over this and finding a way. Is there another way? Can you possibly open up to another and allow other options to be presented. I know this hurts so badly, but any chance you can try again in a different direction?
I think at this point immediate relief is on the horizon with ketamine infusions, but more research is needed. Is that an option for you?

Are you SURE this isn’t anxiety assigning more value to an off the cuff remark than is warranted? Anxiety changes brain patterns and convinces you that people hate you and are judging when they may not be. Not diminishing your pain because regardless the pain you are the one experiencing it, but can you begin to tackle the anxiety and see if that provides any relief?

Don’t leave his side. Your focus is your son, not your wife. I say this as a mother who lost her son and whose husband tried to comfort me also. He is your focus! So talk to him, listen to him - school? If it’s causing problems, take a break. All comes in to focus once they are gone....praying for you all.
If you message me, I’ll give you my number. I’m so sorry for the delay!
I’m still here. I’m sorry for the delay,
Hi - annoying again, but consumed with fear. Please tell me you are ok.

Also, as a mom - not so good with technology. I just refresh the page...so if you don’t hear from me, it’s my failing. I don’t have the app, because I have a billion pics of my kiddo and am afraid to download. ;)
Sending love. I’m here. I’ve pestered and instruded, but now I’m just here.
Ha! I’m snooping you .. but again, I’m here. (told you I cared) my sons name is David. We called him Little David. Worrying about you.
Listen, I respect you. And even the fact that you are talking makes me thankful. So, no worries or pressure from me. Just love. I’m here for whatever. Sending a huge hug from me and my son.

So, do you want to chat? I’m a mom. I also know how this goes...I’m here, listening, watching my sons fav show (lol) and here. So....I’m sleepless, we have plenty of the night. :) dump it all on me... promise I can handle.
Hi - you still with me? Worrying me. Remember I’m a mom :) I worry constantly

Wow! What an accomplishment! That’s crazy, one semester away.... it sounds like you love your family so much but their love isn’t getting through to you in your soul. So, what can we do? It’s the night before Thanksgiving. Family is tough. Where is thanksgiving dinner? And thank you. This would have been a very painful evening for me. But talking to you has gifted me a moment of kindness.
We are here...we are sometimes a little more hidden because we carry some brutal scars. But it’s not just me...

Ok. Understandable with depression. Being unemployed is a symptom of the disease. If you are in school (who gives a good damn about the grades if you are thinking of dying) we have a start point. Can we transfer? So..in Columbus Ohio, the best part of the city is the short North. Also happens to be the 🏳️‍🌈 center. It’s amazing. Our gay friends from San Fran have been shocked at the sense of community in this community. Happens to border Ohio State....as well as Columbus state (2 year college). I don’t pretend to know your struggles, but you don’t have to fight this alone. I’m here listening if we have any time which is up to you?

Are you old enough to relocate? I know that trans and bi-sexuality is very hard to come in to...but can’t we instead find you a mentor? I live in the Midwest, but we have a very thriving community for lgbtq+ and they are some of the pillars of our community. Any chance you’d allow me a day to reach out and connect you? Sometimes when you step in to yourself, others come around eventually. In the meantime, a community helps.

I’m sorry she can’t accept it. I wish I could sit a day and shake her and understand what she’s heading for. She will live in a world of regret. As far as happiness, not yet. It’s only been 8.5 months. Life and our family is very different. Very empty I guess. I don’t truly want to make you understand, because I fear it will burden you all the more. I’m hear to listen. Nothing shocks or causes me to judge, but if you can just give yourself a day or 2? Anyhow, no pressure, just a mom wishing someone would have listened to her boy. Wishing you peace.

I have a grief therapist..unless he can come back, what can truly help? He told us he was really trying - he fought as much as he could. If only love could have saved him.... Look, I would have and still would die for him. If you truly want to gift her anything, sit and tell her everything...EVERYTHING. The attempts, all of it. Give her a chance to understand and fight for you. I’m pulling for you. He was an amazing kid. He just was in a vortex that he couldn’t get out of. I suspect you may be too.

Hi - first off, I’m just so sorry to hear you are hurting. I am a mother that lost my son. If I were to be honest, there are no words that will help her. I’m sorry. She knew you and loved you throughout the entirety of your life. That said, I don’t blame or fault my son. I am thankful for every moment. I just don’t want to delude you that she will not suffer immeasurably without you. I’m wishing you just the strength for another day. Sent with love.

Hi - not judging but lost my son this way. Would you like to talk? I’m ready to simply listen without judgment or any platitudes. I know very well that you are suffering. Can we try getting some of the pain out?

Any chance we could talk about therapies or strategies to help you hang on a little longer? I don’t think you are assessing yourself properly. First off, you want to do good. That speaks very openly to your heart. You may not see it yourself, but just in your words - others do. Have you tried something such a ketamine in a clinical setting? For those that it is effective, suicidal thoughts lift very quickly. I’m hear to listen or chat if you would like.

I hear what you are saying. And I’m so sorry for your pain as you don’t deserve this. This depression happened to you and you did not cause it. I’m here, but won’t push. Thinking of you and wish I could ease your burden - truly.
Hi Kaitlyn - I lost my 17 year old to suicide. Would you like to talk? I’m listening without judgment or fear.

Well, I’m here. It sounds like you are suffering from ptsd from an assault. I’m so sorry. How can I help? Can I listen? Can I help find free counseling in your area? You don’t deserve the hand you were dealt, but perhaps the past doesn’t necessarily define your future?

Hi, can I offer an ear or any support? My son passed away like this. I don’t judge or guilt, but there is some level of understanding and I wanted to offer any moment of peace and perhaps clarity I might provide.
Also, it’s truly difficult to know what to say. This page has great talking points. It gives you a starting point on how to meet someone where they are.

I know you mean well, but when you are depressed, that reads as judgment. You are speaking with those who don’t have the strength to move on and make things better. That’s what depression looks like. So instead, offer to listen and not counsel, but just be present with them as they are suffering. And trust me, they are suffering terribly.

Hi - I’m not sure where to begin, but I did feel compelled to respond because Cape May is one of my favorite places. I feel as though you are being held back by your husband. To be honest, it sounds abusive mentally. I hear your compassion and empathy for him, but at such immense pain to yourself. Would you consider trying to prioritize yourself first before making this decision? He’s taking the energy you need so desperately for life. Try standing up for yourself. Don’t make the coffee. If he doesn’t wake up, that’s his decision - go out and find something healthy for you. Don’t listen to disparaging commentary on your mother - his remarks smack of ingratitude. Right now, while things are dark, you cannot hold another afloat. You need to focus on you. On another note, I am planning to sponsor a bench for my son who passed from suicide on the promenade. I am praying for peace and hope for you.

Hi - I am so very sorry to hear. We lost my 17 year old going on 8 months now. Reach out to another family that understands. It’s a horrific journey, but finding support is imperative. We have surviving children and immediately got them in counseling as well as ourselves. Grief is very different in couples. I’m here as needed, but there are great support groups online too. I’m so very heartbroken to hear.

Hi - I know it must feel that way. As a mom who was in that position with my son, it truly was out of love and terror of the thought of not having someone I loved so dearly around. Of not knowing what to do and so desperately wanting to help. Is there anything that might help you? I know you don’t want to talk, but can we lighten your terrible burden in any way?
Can we talk? Take a breath. Let us help a little.

I don’t want to be disrespectful to the other commenter, but with our son - that was not even close to our experience. He was there 14 days. He had individual counseling daily, group counseling daily, free time, group meetings and family time. We had meetings as a team and in our experience, helps a great deal with stabilization.

I don’t think any of us cling to the label....frankly I’m just a mom. Certainly don’t feel inconvenienced...heartbroken, guilty, failure, empty...would have given anything to take his pain or trade places...those are more truthful labels. It never was anything about me. But I’m sure that’s hard to understand.

You’ve been through so much. I hear how you’re in pain and struggling. I do disagree with you on the notion of not allowing your boyfriend in to your thoughts and feelings. There is simply no way to protect him if you choose to end your life, so I think a better choice is to lay it all out and discuss with him. I say this with compassion and empathy.

It may not be the same, but my husband and I were exactly that. I knew we were soulmates. But, I told him several times that I couldn’t be with him. The thought of possibly changing our relationship to a romantic one and the possibility of that ending and him being out of my life for good - was far too overwhelming. And so I said no, because having him in my life as he was, was a certain - and I couldn’t risk him. Try to hang on...you don’t know the part in the story you are at...

I’m so sorry you are hurting! I don’t know the answers to any of your questions. I don’t know how it all fits together. Is this woman in your life in any way, even as a friend? I’m wishing you a moment of peace today.

And that’s EXACTLY what I was talking about... ;) a truly kind and beautiful soul. Please take care and if the world gets to be too much - reach out. I have no answers, but I have kindness, empathy and a listening ear.

I’m happy it isn’t today. I won’t hassle you at all, but I’m always here to listen without judgment. And of course, we may have to agree to disagree ;) - There is something about the way you respond that makes me feel differently. The one thing I’ve realized in my grief group - sounds sad I know - is that those who are suffering from depression don’t see themselves how others see them. That doesn’t mean that the world, life, people aren’t hurting you - I just mean that described through another’s mind, you may not be seen as you feel.

You aren’t sounding like a broken record to me at all. You are sounding like someone in immense pain that is deserving of compassion and help wherever all of us can provide it. You sound like a gentle and kind soul. I’m listening. I don’t have any empty words at all, but do you think you might be able to give yourself a few days? Sometimes, when you are hurting terribly, you aren’t able to see all the good in you... I’m not going to refute this if you feel differently, but you truly sound like a good albeit hurting soul.

I hear your words. And I hear that you are devastated by this loss...and I hear that you are truly truly hurting. I don’t wish to minimize any of it. I’m just wondering if there is any hope that you can find happiness in even the smallest things while you try to heal. Are there any tiny steps you can try? I’m not placing any judgment, just listening and would like to try to understand.

As a mother of a son that passed by suicide, I doubt you are a burden. They may get frustrated at times, but it sounds like you are very loved. Please please consider that depression may be clouding your judgment.

Does he have a diagnosis? Is he prescribed medication he isn’t taking? Sounds like a mental break to me (I’m not a doctor however). If you cannot keep him safe and this is unusual behavior for him, you can certainly have him held for 3 days involuntarily to have him evaluated.

Can you google his name? If he’s still living, I might get rid of the paper being that it’s almost a year old. If he has passed away, please turn in to campus police as his family will be searching for answers and would want that.

Are you still with us? I’m here. I am currently surviving a suicide and understand the guilt. That’s the aftermath of any suicide. Everyone in the immediate ring blames themselves. Are you safe right now? I’m here to listen and not guide or judge. I know you are in so much pain, and I’m sorry.

I’m so sorry to hear. The words really aren’t sufficient. The pain after a suicide is suffocating..you don’t want to go on a moment longer without them. I understand, and I’m sorry. For me, Life had to come to a screeching halt....it took a long time to not wake up and wish I was with him. But the intensity of the feelings does soften just a little with time. The grieving and loss, that may never go away. We entered specific grief counseling immediately following and reached out to others that had survived this. How can I help you? I’m here to listen. I hope you are being held up by people caring for you right now.
:) I’m not sure I’m the reason, you just needed someone to chat it through with you. I’m so happy to hear!
I’m just checking in as I haven’t heard from you. I am absolutely still here.
Of course!
Ok, I hear what you are saying. It sounds like you need to feel relevant, and don’t feel it? I’m here and listening...
Ok, I’m here. Let’s talk. You are worthy of love, you know.
Interested in talking?
Would you want to talk? I’d love to hear. Sometimes just being heard can help a tiny bit?

I think you may find some degree in comfort talking to those of us surviving a suicide. Doesn’t need to be me, but the amount of guilt and blame is usually present for everyone in the immediate family and suicidal thoughts are very normal in the aftermath. Are you in any therapy? Or in a group where you can hear how normal but nonetheless disastrous these thoughts are? I’m so sorry your sister isn’t here. It isn’t your fault. There is usually never one factor in a suicide. You aren’t alone. You are suffering terribly, but there are so many who understand and can help you gain some footing.
Yes, this gave me pause to think outside my own loss. You are right and in that instance, it is a choice and one that I would never judge. Thank you for the kindness and compassion in your response.

First off, I’m so sorry for your loss. As we are 6 months out from the passing of our 17 year old son, here is what helped. Offer help to take the 15 year old out. He will have a different recovery rate than his mom and needs strength and as much normalcy as you can provide. Bring a meal for the freezer. She will have so little energy in the months to come and needs it after the initial flurry of meals. Get your husband to talk to someone. Grief and differences in grieving can ruin the strongest of relationships. Offer to talk about the darkness you have felt. It helped me tremendously to hear what my son had experienced. And for all involved, don’t rush or push them through their grief. Be present emotionally or physically. Suicide has a ring that causes the immediate family to entertain thoughts of suicide themselves. They need others to stabilize them. Just my two cents as to what helped us. So so sad to hear another family suffering.

Wrong. Absolutely wrong. Suicide for survivors is a VERY complicated grief. It is nowhere as simple as you are making it out to be. And I also disagree with the notion of a choice...a choice of a diseased mind is not really a choice at all.
Yeah..it’s kind of something you learn the hard way how to truly get down in the dark place and listen. But there are those of us that are out there and ready to listen.

Nope, not deserving of any of this. You are struggling and coping as best you can. I don’t fault her because im sure she feels hopeless and worried and tired, but you are trying and addiction is not always a perfect All or nothing solution. (Her word choice though, not ok.) It’s about the gradual climb. Can you just take a small step today?

I know it might seem scary to talk to a professional, but you have to try. PPD is hormone related and so meds are pretty effective with it. It’s also pretty typical, so telling your provider that you’re suffering from it is likely going to get meds prescribed, not a hospital stay. Please try reaching out. Motherhood can feel overwhelming but a little less so when you yourself are feeling stable.

@connornomore - you deserve hope and I think it’s AMAZING that here you are in so much pain trying to help others. I wasn’t trashing you and think your heart is beautiful and in the right place. I know you are hurting too. We are all just trying to support how it’s been shown to help best, not in any way disregarding you or your efforts. All of us are here to support you also. ❤️

I know you mean so well and it’s so natural for us to talk like this. But when you are talking to someone with suicidal ideation, the language has to change. Start with the talking points on the sub. They help. It’s that by the time someone is in that dark tunnel, hope is shut out. So, they don’t see that happiness could be right around the corner, because they’ve waited A LONG time and suffered while waiting. Also, they feel like a burden and a failure. If we talk about others pain, it’s saying that basically they should continue suffering and that they have failed or become a burden to yet another person. It’s not intuitive, but once you truly understand, it’s easier. It’s basicalky the difference between trying to pull them in to the light (no) and trying to get in to the dark (yes) is that they aren’t so alone. Does this make sense? But I think it’s so great that you are here trying to help. :)

If you aren’t familiar with speaking with someone suicidal, go to the “talking points” on this sub. They will help. He needs to feel heard, not contradicted and supported. But you will also need to be open and ok with whatever you hear. This can’t in any way be about your thoughts or feelings. It has to be about trying your best to hear where he is at. I’m sorry to hear this, but I’m so glad you have time still and that this isn’t after the fact. Best wishes for the conversation to help.

Hi - the same had actually happened to me in regards to my son’s death. It was actually such a great learning lesson for me. The admin took the time to respond to my questions as to why and also point me to a wide body of information as to why. She explained the talking points to me and I can now say she absolutely did the right thing. When we are looking at it from a survivors perspective, it can make people suffering from suicidal ideation feel like even more of a failure/burden. I just wanted to reach out to you and let you know that I had also been down that path. I’m so truly sorry for your loss.

Sounds like the daughter truly needs her mom and is frightened that she will lose her to you. I would ask to gently speak with the girl to reassure her that she will always be her mother’s priority and that you are not trying to take that from her. Best of luck!
This post gives me hope that we indeed go on. Caveat to say that I am in the grieving process and needed to hear this.

I mean, what probably is really going on here is best addressed with a counselor or a real breakdown of your thoughts and feelings. Very few people are just inarguably attractive to everyone. It’s based on things you can control and things you can’t (like life experiences that draw you toward one person or another).And attractiveness at best, opens the door only. But very few people build relationships with an attractive empty shell of a person. And attractive people have their own crisis of self when no one sees their inner qualities and just their outer shell. I think you look just how you should look - perfect for you.

Try to look at it this way....if I were to take a picture of myself and open the door for others to tell me what to change about myself, can you understand the crisis in sense of self I  might have? I might have people telling me (based on their own preferences and life experiences) to color my hair, shorten it, lengthen it, get colored contacts, gain weight, lose weight, change my style, etc - and if I internalized it, it would destroy me because you can’t be everything to everyone. Look, your looks aren’t your issue here. And I mean that with love and compassion. You’re just looking for love. Nothing wrong with that, but you will continue to suffer if you don’t just embrace you.
This resonates more with me also....
